messages:
Bob R.: morning all, Bob here — first week. i used the sandbox key from onboarding but want to run a few streaming experiments and a small traffic sweep. what's the recommended path to get a dev/hosted key and avoid hitting 429s? also any security gotchas (rotating, env vars)?

Priya: welcome Bob :wave: Fastest is Console -> Settings -> API keys -> New key (choose Hosted). Sandbox keys from the email are temporary and intentionally limited. Hosted keys are tied to billing and have higher quotas. If your UI is missing options, tag #eng-platform.

InfraBot: Reminder: creating or deleting hosted keys emits an audit event. Keys should be created per-project and rotated regularly.

Bob R.: nice. can i script creation from my linux box? i'd like a reproducible dev key creation flow for my repo bootstrap.

Diego: yes — we have an internal CLI `redwoodctl` (dev-only) for automation. example:
```
# create a hosted key for a dev project
redwoodctl keys create --env hosted --name="bob-autocomplete-dev" --expires="7d"
```
It uses your SSO auth. If you hit 403, post the request in #eng-platform and include your org + GitHub team so they can grant the role.

Priya: quick security tips: store the key in your local secrets manager or set REDWOOD_HOSTED_KEY in your dev env (dont commit to git). rotate keys if you suspect leakage. enable “restrict by origin” if you accidentally use in client-side demos.

Maya: for streaming-specific stuff: prefer a single long-lived stream/socket and multiplex messages, use client-side token accounting (track how many tokens you send per minute), and implement exponential backoff + jitter on 429s. Avoid opening new sockets for each request.

Bob R.: sandbox is pretty small for multi-hour sweeps. what's the workflow to request a temporary quota bump for a one-off test?

Diego: post in #eng-platform with: project name, billing owner, exact UTC start/end, peak tokens/min (or total tokens), expected concurrency. Example we like to see: project: autocomplete-playground; billing: @Priya; window: 2026-04-02T15:00Z->2026-04-02T17:00Z; peak: 250k tokens/hour; concurrency: ~20. Temporary increases are typically 24-72h.

eng-platform: acknowledged. we'll need the billing owner to confirm and we'll check capacity. response time usually within one business day. we may provide a scoped key with controlled rate limits.

Bob R.: are there headers or metrics i can watch client-side to detect approaching limits before infra returns 429s?

Maya: yes, watch any rate-limit headers the SDK surfaces (e.g., X-RateLimit-Remaining style headers) and instrument tokens/min in your client. If you see remaining tokens drop rapidly, throttle proactively. Also log and surface 429s with the retry-after info.

Priya: one more ops trick: run a short warmup at low concurrency to prime caches and model weights, then ramp gradually. that reduces cold-start variability and gives you faster feedback without burning quota.

Bob R.: thanks — last Q: can hosted keys be scoped to read-only vs full usage? i'd prefer safer defaults for dev keys.

Diego: currently keys support project scoping and expiry; we're rolling out usage-scoped keys soon. in the meantime, create short-lived keys (expires=7d) and rotate. if you need more constraints, ask eng-platform and security for a scoped dev token.

InfraBot: Tip: label keys with project and owner so teams can audit them easily.

Bob R.: perfect — i'll open the #eng-platform request with the window and billing owner. thanks everyone! :heart:
